docs#OrderHom is using docs#Monotone, while docs#OrderEmbedding and docs#OrderIso are abbrevs for docs#RelEmbedding and docs#RelIso with (· ≤ ·).
Should we change OrderHom to an abbrev for docs#RelHom with (· ≤ ·)?
(the two definitions are Equiv of course)
cc @Yaël Dillies
I would rather have us go the other way around, so that the fields can be properly named and use LE-only predicates, like docs#Monotone. @Wrenna Robson has thought about this before

Do we have a def for a ≤ b ↔ f a ≤ f b? I don't know of one.
In a LinearOrder this is StrictMono f (docs#StrictMono.le_iff_le, docs#strictMono_of_le_iff_le) but not generally.
Monotone uses Preorder, no? Or are you saying that's the one you'd change?
No, we do not, but @Patrick Massot has argued in the past that this is what docs#StrictMono should mean (or that StrictMono should be used much less in favor of the currently missing predicate)
I have looked at it before and I'm interested in helping to fix it, but it's a little bit of a tangle for sure.
btw #38557 weakens Preorder to LE in Monotone

Yaël Dillies said:

No, we do not, but Patrick Massot has argued in the past that this is what docs#StrictMono should mean (or that StrictMono should be used much less in favor of the currently missing predicate)

I actually forgot that this wasn't what it meant. It probably is what it should mean yeah.

Snir Broshi said:

#38557 weakens Monotone from Preorder to LE btw

Would you consider also changing SortedLE, SortedLT etc. in this? I created them because having names for essentially those specific cases was useful.

(though there you do want to use LT rather than the iff condition - not quite sure how you translate that nicely to lists. Anyway it would be convenient to maintain this change for the definition even if in practice most theorems will need it.)
Honestly in practice, when do you ever need LT when it's not at least a lawfulorderLT? You see why the preorder condition is so useful here.

Snir Broshi said:

Do we have a def for a ≤ b ↔ f a ≤ f b? I don't know of one.
In a LinearOrder this is StrictMono f (docs#StrictMono.le_iff_le, docs#strictMono_of_le_iff_le) but not generally.

this feels like a sort of order-inducing condition, similar to Topology.isInducing_iff (where a function is inducing when sets in the domain are open iff they are preimages of opens)?
so this could be called IsOrderInducing
We certainly have at least the bundled version docs#OrderEmbedding.
And indeed this is the meaningful condition for partial orders.

For people who never thought about this, here are two fun exercises:

  • StrictMono f does not imply that f is injective.
  • StrictMono f and Bijective f together do not imply order embedding (ie ∀ a b, a ≤ b ↔ f a ≤ f b)

Snir Broshi said:

docs#OrderHom is using docs#Monotone, while docs#OrderEmbedding and docs#OrderIso are abbrevs for docs#RelEmbedding and docs#RelIso with (· ≤ ·).
Should we change OrderHom to an abbrev for docs#RelHom with (· ≤ ·)?
(the two definitions are Equiv of course)

I just got bitten by this in #40515. #synth Monoid (α →o α) failed, so I decided to add the instance. I also did Group (α ≃o α), which Eric then asked me to generalize to Group (r ≃r r) since it's an abbrev. I did, and then the build failed because we already have this instance. Of course, we have the one or RelHom too, but because α →o α isn't an abbrev, it didn't apply.
@Yaël Dillies can you expand on why you think we should move away from abbrevs here? I don't see the field names of the structure as being terribly important.
I think the argument is that having the structure field be of type Monotone is handy
But this isn't a very good argument, because the field type is wrong anyway due to FunLike.coeFn, and so is a primed internal-ish name
Hypothetically, we could make the generalisation of Monotone for relations, and make Monotone the abbrev?
This has probably a huge performance cost
That would be the bigger of the possible refractors though, since we're touching the relHom hierarchy instead of just orderhom

Yaël Dillies said:

This has probably a huge performance cost

Why do you think so?
because then LE would appear twice in the type, instead of just once, and `Monotone is used in a lot of places
When does it ever appear once?
Monotone takes two order instances?
you need both the domain and the codomain to be ordered
